policies.title: Aruba: named ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government list expressly exempts these nationalities for Aruba. Jamaica is separately stated to require a visa for Aruba.
conditions: The policy is a short visitor baseline; passport validity, onward travel, purpose, funds, insurance, health, security and border-admission requirements continue to apply.

Hong Kong entries require either a British National (Overseas) or SAR passport; Macao entries require an SAR passport; Taiwan requires a passport bearing its identity-card number; Ukraine requires a biometric passport.
No residence, work, transit, crew, cruise, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, third-country visa/residence-permit or other special-document rule is normalized.
For Aruba, general visa-free stay is up to 90 days in 180; Dutch, US and non-Dutch Schengen nationals may have stated 180-day allowances.

policies.title: Curaçao: named ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government list expressly exempts these nationalities for Curaçao, including its Curaçao-only Jamaica rule.
conditions: The policy is a short visitor baseline; passport validity, onward travel, purpose, funds, insurance, health, security and border-admission requirements continue to apply.

Hong Kong entries require either a British National (Overseas) or SAR passport; Macao entries require an SAR passport; Taiwan requires a passport bearing its identity-card number; Ukraine requires a biometric passport.

For Curaçao, the general visa-free stay is up to 90 days in 180; Dutch and US nationals have the stated 180-day allowance.

policies.title: Aruba: residual ordinary passports require a Caribbean visa
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government page supplies an explicit residual visa requirement after the named nationality and conditional exceptions; this is advance Caribbean-visa treatment, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current official portal explicitly makes a Caribbean visa required if no listed visa-free situation applies; an application channel does not establish eVisa or visa-on-arrival access.

Valid multiple-entry Schengen/UK/Ireland/US/Canada documents and specified residence permits may waive the visa for particular travellers; these conditional routes are not nationality-wide passport classifications.
The Caribbean short-stay visa is not valid for the European Netherlands or another Schengen country, is normally at most 90 days in 180, and does not authorize paid work.
Aruba's maximum stay on a visa can be up to 180 consecutive days within 365, subject to the issued visa.
